result:
The lower bound holds. For $P_6$, one vertex covers at most 3 consecutive vertices, so $\iota(P_6)=2$. Subdividing 3 edges gives $P_9$, where $S=\{v_3,v_7\}$ leaves $\{v_1,v_5,v_9\}$ independent, so $\iota=2$ is unchanged. Subdividing 4 edges gives $P_{10}$, where two closed neighborhoods cover at most 6 vertices, leaving 4 uncovered vertices in at most 3 gaps, so $\iota(P_{10})=3$. Hence $\mathrm{sd}_\iota(P_6)=4$, and the maximum is at least 4.

The upper bound is less certain. The argument that a pendant path of length $\ge 4$ gives $\mathrm{sd}_\iota\le 4$ is reasonable, since the periodicity $g(m+4)=g(m)+1$ shifts every boundary configuration by exactly 1. The bushy-tree case, where all pendant paths have length at most 3, is only checked on a few examples (e.g., $S(2,2,2)$ needs at most 1), not proved in general. I did not find a tree needing 5, but I have not ruled one out either.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
CONFIDENCE: 3
